note: خواہ is primarily a conjunction/discourse word meaning whether/or, even if, or whether...or. 'Soliciting' and suffix POS are not appropriate core analyses.
معاہدے is an inflected form of معاہدہ and must explicitly give agreements/treaties/agreement rather than only inflection labels.
رحیم means merciful/compassionate and is also the name Rahim; the current 'very merciful' is acceptable but incomplete for ordinary name usage.
دماغ centrally means brain/mind/intellect. 'Conceit, pride' is idiomatic/peripheral and should not lead the general learner entry.
مبارک means blessed/auspicious and is used in congratulations ('congratulations!/happy ...'). The source's English wording is awkward and should be normalized.
proposed_english: blessed; auspicious; congratulations!; happy (as in Happy Birthday/Eid, context-dependent)

note: ہار is a major homograph: defeat/loss, necklace/garland, and the verb stem/imperative of ہارنا meaning lose/give up. The source lists only defeat/loss.
proposed_english: defeat; loss; necklace; garland; lose!/give up (verb stem, context-dependent)

note: مری is the feminine singular perfect form meaning died and is also Murree, the place name. 'Closed-class' is incorrect.
The standard Urdu spelling is دعویٰ. The word means claim/assertion and can mean legal claim/lawsuit. The current unmarked final alif-maqsura spelling is less precise for a learner workbook.
پہ is a colloquial/variant form of پر meaning on/at/upon. A learner entry should give the direct English meaning rather than only 'synonym of پر'.
proposed_english: on; at; upon (variant/colloquial form of پر)

note: ذرا means a little/slightly/just and is often a politeness softener ('please/just...'). 'Petit' is French dictionary contamination.
proposed_english: a little; slightly; just; please/just (politeness softener)

note: ہفتہ centrally means week and can also mean Saturday; in colloquial South Asian usage hafta can mean an extortion/protection payment. The source omits 'week' entirely.
کلب in modern Urdu is the English loan 'club'. 'Dog' reflects an Arabic/literary homograph کَلْب and should not be presented unqualified in the standard Urdu entry.

جناح is extremely common as the proper name/surname Jinnah in Urdu, especially Muhammad Ali Jinnah; it also has the Arabic-derived noun sense wing/flank. The source omits the proper-name meaning despite name POS.
سود means interest (on money)/profit/usury. 'Content word' is not a POS.
شکایت centrally means complaint/grievance/objection and can refer to a medical complaint/symptom. The entry should lead with the normal general meaning.
داد means praise/appreciation/applause and, in legal/literary usage, justice/redress. 'Content word' is not a POS.
بہن centrally means sister. Female cousin or a respectful address for another woman can occur contextually, but 'any female person' is too broad.
proposed_english: sister; female cousin (context-dependent); respectful address for a woman (context-dependent)

note: خام centrally means raw/unripe/crude/unfinished and can mean rough/approximate. The source omits the basic 'raw' meaning and adds misleading 'smaller/lower'.
proposed_english: raw; unripe; crude; unfinished; rough; approximate

note: نگرانی centrally means supervision/monitoring/oversight/watch. 'Security' is context-dependent and should not replace these core senses.
قید is a noun meaning imprisonment/confinement/captivity/restriction. 'Captive' is an English adjective/noun and is not the best direct gloss for the Urdu noun.
چلی is very commonly the feminine singular perfect form of چلنا meaning went/left/moved, and the same spelling is used for Chile. Name-only POS is incorrect.
proposed_english: went; left; moved (feminine singular form of چلنا); Chile (country)

note: ساڑھے is a numerical quantifier meaning and a half/half past, used with numbers (especially 3 and above). Adjective alone is not the clearest POS.
proposed_english: and a half; half past (used with numbers)
